newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mixed, November up on spreading.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mixed, November up on spreading.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mixed, with November underpinned by continued bull spreading, CME floor traders said.
"There just doesn't seem to be a way to break November right now," one dealer said.

Bulls continued to bet that lumber data expected to be released by the Canadian government Thursday will show that Canadian mills are nearing their export quotas so near-term supplies will diminish sharply, traders and analyts said.
Activity in lumber futures Tuesday was characterized as quiet as the trade waited for quota and new homes data.
"We're just waiting around for the numbers," one pit trader said. "That's why the market is just laying around."
U.S. new home sales data for September will be released at 0900 CST/1500 GMT, and the trade is looking for the data to show a dip, one lumber analyst said.
According to a consensus of analysts, the new home sales data should fall in range of 735,000 to 810,000 new homes.
A quiet tone in cash lumber markets also contributed to slight weakness in deferred lumber contracts, traders said.
CME November lumber futures closed up $1.00 at $422.20 per thousand board feet. January ended down $3.60 at $384.40. Other contracts settled down $2.10 to $4.00 tbf.
